¿Cómo se calcula el precio de un bono?: How is the price of a bond calculated?
Es el valor actual de sus flujos descont: It is the present value of its cash flows discounted at the yield to maturity. A €1,000 bond with a 5 % coupon over 3 years and a yield of 4 % pays 50, 50 and 1,050: 50/1.04 + 50/1.04² + 1,050/1.04³ ≈ €1,027.75.
¿Qué mide la duración de un bono?: What does a bond's duration measure?
La duración de Macaulay es el plazo medi: Macaulay duration is the average time, weighted by present value, in which the investment is recovered: in the example above, about 2.86 years. Divided by (1 + yield) it gives the modified duration, which indicates how much the price falls for each point the yield rises.

Si el cupón es mayor que la TIR, el bono: If the coupon is greater than the yield, the bond is worth more than its face value (above par); if smaller, less (below par); if they coincide, it is worth exactly the face value. Price and yield move in opposite directions.
Es el plazo medio ponderado en que se re: It is the weighted average time in which the investment is recovered, weighting each cash flow by its present value: $D = ∑ t·PV_t / P$. It is measured in years; it is less than the maturity if there are coupons, and equal to it for a zero-coupon bond.
$D_m = D/(1 + y/m)$ da la sensibilidad d: $D_m = D/(1 + y/m)$ gives the sensitivity of the price to the yield: $ΔP/P ≈ −D_m·Δy$. The longer the duration, the more the bond falls when rates rise.
La relación precio-TIR no es una recta,: The price-yield relationship is not a line but a convex curve. Convexity $C$ corrects the duration approximation: $ΔP/P ≈ −D_m·Δy + ½·C·Δy²$. With it the estimate gets much closer to the exact price, especially for large changes.
